walkthroughs.body_html:
Programming Fundamentals — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Programming Fundamentals brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Programming Fundamentals.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler is a person, an interpreter is software.
A compiler translates the whole program first; an interpreter executes line by line.
The computer crashes.
They produce different programming languages.
Having multiple classes with the same name.
The ability of different classes to respond to the same method call in their own way.
The computer crashes.
Variables that change type at runtime.

mcqs.q: What happens when 11111111 + 1 is computed in an 8-bit register?
options: The computer crashes.
Variables that change type at runtime.
It just becomes 100000000 normally.
Overflow - the result requires 9 bits but only 8 are available.
